name: derailment coefficient
domain: 车辆轨道基础结构动力学

complete_examples.text: To guarantee the safety, comfort and stability of the running vehicle in the presence of track profile deformations, several dynamic indices, including car body accelerations, wheel-rail forces, wheel-rail relative displacements, wheel unloading rate and derailment coefficient, will be adopted to evaluate the irregularity limits.
Taking the 1st wheelset, as an instance, the calculated derailment coefficient at different vehicle speed is shown in Fig. 24.
It can be seen from the results that the max derailment coefficient is distributed near the 47 m, which is similar to the jump derailment location shown in Fig. 24(b) and (c).
The derailment coefficient is defined as the ratio of lateral and vertical wheel-rail forces, which is an index to judge the safety of wheelset derailment [47].
It can be observed that the response or index decreases with the long-term temperature rise, except for the derailment coefficient.
When the fault displacement is 30 mm and 40 mm with train speed below 200 km/h, the derailment coefficient changes in the range of 0.16–0.55 in P-PRBT and 0.14– 0.54 in CRTS III.
It is noted that in P-PRBT, under fault dislocation of 30 mm and 40 mm, when the vehicle speed reaches 200 km/h, the derailment coefficient reaches 0.89 and 0.92, which exceeds the safety standard.

Additionally, under the excitation of the debris flows, the maximum derailment coefficient of the vehicle can reach 0.88, indicating that it exceeds the safety limit of derailment coefficient and poses a threat to the train operation safety.
M. CHEN ET AL. derailment coefficient is below the safety limit, and the vehicle can operate safely.

At different seismic intensities, the wheel-rail lateral force and the wheel-rail vertical force reach the maximum at 0.40g, which are 46.760 1 kN and 94.863 7 kN, respectively, and increase by 182.68% and 5.35%, respectively, compared with 0.35g, and the derailment coefficient increases by 168.28% compared with 0.35g. The vibration of the soil body during the earthquake shows an amplification effect, and the modulus of soil body is higher than the magnification coefficient, which is very large.
